artifacts.title: Tail Certificates and Achievement-Set Geometry for Erdős Problems 249 and 257
artifacts.claim_scope: Gateway exposition for Erdős Problems 249 and 257. For #249 it records the exact dyadic-section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1, infinite-dimensionality, the explicit finite Farey denominator exclusion, and diagonal certificates through t = 82, but no instance at t = 83 or unbounded family. For #257 it records checked restricted-support geometry and the remaining half-value and 1/21 branches. Both problems remain open, and the shared Lambert-series change of variables transfers no irrationality theorem.

artifacts.title: The Binary Totient Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 249. It distinguishes checked premises and finite certificates from open obligations: the level-e dyadic-section rank is 2^e+1 only for e >= 1; the full span is infinite-dimensional; the finite Farey computation excludes denominators up to the stated bound; and diagonal certificates exist through t = 82, with neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 257. It gives complete ordinary arguments and records Lean proofs of the finite-prime weighted criterion, its hereditary base-two-host/all-base consequence, the strengthened positive-cover criterion, the common-scale mixed weighted/cover criterion, and the reciprocal-summable-support corollary without pairwise coprimality. Each theorem retains its stated infinitude, positivity, weighted-mass, cover-majorant, scaled-cost, host-containment, and common-witness hypotheses as applicable. The named separating examples and their divergent-reciprocal calculations are ordinary mathematics and are not themselves replayed in Lean. The record separately retains checked finite-support and restricted achievement-set structure: no finite rank-at-least-two support represents 1/21, while the eventual affine-supercapacity regime survives. The universal, half-value, and 1/21 membership questions remain open.

artifacts.title: Bases and Integral Relations for the $k$-Kernel of Euler's Totient
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 249, ordered unconditional results first: the exact level-e dyadic totient section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1 (Lean) and the resulting infinite-dimensionality, which for integer-valued sequence modules is equivalent to Coons's non-k-regularity and is not an independent contribution; the all-base exact-rank upgrade uses Martin's external independence hypothesis. A separate ordinary argument treats bounded-residue series A_m. The explicit finite-Farey denominator exclusion and Lean diagonal certificates through t = 82 are finite; neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family is supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Weighted Support Criteria for Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 257. Lean proves the finite-prime weighted support criterion, its hereditary base-two-host/all-base consequence, the strengthened positive-cover criterion under its cover-majorant and summable scaled-cost hypotheses, and the mixed weighted/cover criterion using a common observation scale. Lean also proves that summable reciprocal-support mass suffices without pairwise coprimality. The named examples separating these criteria, including the displayed divergent-reciprocal host, use ordinary set and summability calculations and are not separately replayed as Lean theorems. These sufficient criteria retain their stated support hypotheses and do not cover arbitrary infinite supports. The universal, half-value, and 1/21 membership questions remain open; cited classical results and attribution remain distinct from local proof provenance.

artifacts.title: Two Incomparable Denominator Exclusions\\for $\sum_{n\ge2}(n!-1)^{-1}$
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos68 modules. The Comparator isolation pin for the carry equivalences is FactorialGapPlateauCore; FactorialZeroPlateau is the default-root duplicate of that family, not the isolation source. Lean checks the exact factorial-successor and eventual-unit-carry frontiers, integral-channel and prime-translator identities, weighted projection consumers, and the Cramer residual identity. An independently regenerated exact GMP certificate supplies one non-unit carry at m = 300000, and a Lean theorem consumes that finite fact to exclude every smaller positive rational denominator; a separate continued-fraction bound gives q ≥ 2^39990. The two finite exclusions are incomparable. No theorem supplies cofinally many non-unit carries; Erdős Problem 68 remains open.

artifacts.title: Bounded Increments and Rational Reciprocal Sums
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos243 modules. Lean checks the integer-state bounded-negative theorem, with eventual strict centring, a bounded negative part, and normalised vanishing remaining explicit hypotheses, together with constant- and periodic-negative exclusions. The original-coordinate LCM/product-defect corollary is an ordinary transfer; PaperCompleteR7/ProductDefect.lean is absent from this checkout. Koizumi supplies normalised vanishing for the canonical orbit; boundedness of its negative part is not supplied. Unbounded upward excursions of the unreduced numerator remain open, so Erdős Problem 243 remains open.

artifacts.title: Sparse Congruence-Preserving Perturbations\\of Dyadic Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos251 module. A sparse perturbation of the prime gaps can have a rational dyadic sum while retaining the prime growth scale, every fixed eventual congruence, and asymptotically the same short-block statistics; the later positions are not asserted to be prime. This is complementary to Land's conditional result, not a refutation. Lean checks an elementary pair-and-buffer core; the full schedule and block-law estimates are ordinary mathematics, not Lean- or Comparator-verified. The prime-to-gap identity is the already-known summation-by-parts (Tao on the forum, 7 October 2025); this checkout checks it, discharging summability by an elementary polynomial prime bound rather than the prime-number theorem. Lean also checks unboundedness and non-eventual-periodicity of the actual prime gaps, and the exact local implication from cofinally recurring adjacent small-mismatch tail shifts to failure of eventual integrality. The tail-shift route requires that condition for every fixed positive h; the h=1 case alone does not complete it. No theorem supplies the required cofinal adjacent small-mismatch pairs, and Erdős Problem 251 remains open.

artifacts.title: No Finite Separable Representation\\at Three Prime Generators
artifacts.claim_scope: Steve Fan posted the two-prime factorisation, reduction and transcendence conclusion first (erdosproblems.com/269, 26 June 2026, post-7218). This paper records that argument as an ordinary deduction from Bugeaud–Laurent's external Hecke–Mahler theorem and does not claim priority or a Lean theorem for the two-prime case. For three primes the paper proves nonsingular selected minors of every order from one binary carry. Comparator checks the (2,3,5) minor −1/15, the running-LCM height identity, and a conditional carry-escape consumer; it does not check the arbitrary-order rank theorem. The actual-series reduction is given; the source-specific cofinal escape remains unproved. Problem 269 remains open from three primes onward.

artifacts.title: Paths in Polynomial Lemniscates:\\Trinomials and Critical-Value Bounds
artifacts.claim_scope: This note gives ordinary proofs for explicit short-path families, led by all-degree monic trinomials. Lean checks Newton-flow value decay and its exponential first integral, oriented-ray separation, common-translation collision geometry, finite affine-line avoidance, root retention under small constant perturbations, cyclic-trinomial spoke/fibre inequalities, and the sharp critical-value mean and its stated finite-degree power budget. These declarations retain their exact hypotheses and do not certify every analytic assembly as one theorem. Lean also checks ani’s explicit monic degree-seven instance: its roots are distinct and lie in the open unit disc, and every continuous path in the strict unit lemniscate between distinct roots has total variation greater than 2. This refutes the stated universal total-variation formulation. The result is one instance, not the reported small-parameter family or a Hausdorff-measure comparison; historical correspondence awaits independent human review. Positive-family results remain valid under their stated hypotheses.

artifacts.title: Zudilin's Forms at Rational Bases\\and the Exact Normalised Hankel Order
artifacts.claim_scope: Lean proves the rational-base region theorem: for natural numbers 0 < b < a in the exact Zudilin contour region, F(a/b) is irrational. In particular, F((31/4)^r) is irrational for every positive natural r. Lean also proves the stated irrationality-exponent bound on this region. For the normalized Zudilin Hankel determinant, Lean proves the order N(N-1)(2N-1)/6 and leading coefficient (N!)²(N+1)!/2^N at every natural rank N, including zero. The region theorem and construction retain their Zudilin attribution; formal verification does not establish novelty. The contour excludes 3/2, so irrationality of F(3/2) and universal Erdős #1049 remain open.

artifacts.title: Paths in Polynomial Lemniscates: Proofs and Examples
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 1041. It assembles ordinary positive-family arguments and exact obstruction examples, alongside Lean-checked Newton-flow and ray-separation results, translation geometry, perturbation, cyclic-trinomial, critical-value-mean and solved-family kernels. It records ani’s checked degree-seven total-variation counterexample: one explicit monic polynomial has distinct open-disc roots and every continuous strict-lemniscate path between distinct roots has variation greater than 2. The result is one instance, not the reported family or a Hausdorff-measure theorem; historical correspondence awaits independent human review. The remaining ordinary analytic assemblies carry no blanket Lean-coverage claim.

artifacts.title: Zudilin's Forms at Rational Bases:\\Proofs and Research Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Reasoning record for Erdős #1049, with the central rational-base region, power-family, irrationality-exponent and all-rank Hankel statements directly Lean-checked. For natural numbers 0 < b < a satisfying the exact Zudilin contour hypothesis, the constructed polynomial forms prove F(a/b) irrational and its irrationality exponent at most rationalBaseMeasureBound(a,b), without a coprimality premise. The power-family consequence gives irrationality for F((31/4)^r) for every positive natural r. Lean identifies the normalized Hankel determinant order N(N-1)(2N-1)/6 and leading coefficient (N!)²(N+1)!/2^N at every rank, closing the previous all-row gap. Zudilin attribution remains explicit; kernel acceptance does not adjudicate novelty. The contour excludes 3/2, and no theorem here proves irrationality at 3/2 or at every rational base greater than one.

artifacts.title: Denominators and Rationality Criteria\\for $\sum_{n\ge2}(n!-1)^{-1}$
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős #68. Lean checks the Core carry equivalences. artifacts.title: Reciprocal-Tail Rigidity: Theorems, Proofs and Questions
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #243. The cubic-rate irrationality theorem is ordinary mathematics, including the Chebotarev step, and is not a Lean endpoint. The established bounded-negative regime is distinct from the remaining unbounded upward excursions of the unreduced numerator. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Prime-Gap Dyadic Series:\\Perturbations, Exact Criteria and Certificates
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #251. The exact prime-to-gap identity does not use the prime-number theorem. The finite counting reduction for shifted prime-gap differences and the countermodel remain the supported contribution; analytic sieve estimates are not a remaining assumption of the identity. The actual-prime tail witness remains open. The problem remains open.

artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #269. The two-prime transcendence argument is Steve Fan's (26 June 2026) and is not a Lean theorem. The actual-series reduction is given; the source-specific cofinal escape remains unproved. The problem remains open.
